evals.prompt:
Here's use case UC-31 'Return an online order' from our analysis doc. Can you derive the test cases? Markdown file please.

Actor: registered customer. Precondition: the customer has a delivered order.
Main success scenario:
1. The customer opens the order in 'My orders' and chooses 'Return items'.
2. The system shows the returnable items of the order.
3. The customer selects one or more items and a return reason.
4. The system checks that each selected item is still within the return window of 30 days after delivery.
5. The system creates a return with a prepaid shipping label and emails the label to the customer.
6. The customer ships the parcel. When the warehouse registers it, the system refunds the item price to the original payment method.
Extensions:
2a. The order contains no returnable items (all items are final sale): the system shows 'Nothing to return' and the use case ends.
3a. The customer selects no item: the system asks to select at least one item and the customer returns to step 3.
4a. An item is outside the return window: the system removes it from the return and tells the customer why. If no items remain, the use case ends.
6a. The warehouse rejects an item as damaged by the customer: the system refunds nothing for that item and notifies the customer.
Postcondition: the refunded amount equals the sum of the accepted items' prices, and the return has status Closed.
evals.expected_output: Path inventory with main path and 2a/3a/4a/6a, one test per path, postconditions on every path, the 30-day window split out as a boundary unit, traceability to UC-31 steps.
assertions: A path inventory lists the main path and all four extensions (2a, 3a, 4a, 6a) with where each branches and where it ends
Every extension path has at least one test case
The 3a loop is tested back to completion (select nothing, then select an item and finish)
The 30-day return window is handled as its own boundary unit with tests on both sides of day 30
Alternate and exception paths check their postconditions or failure guarantees (e.g. no label, no refund, return status), not only the main path
Test cases trace to UC-31 steps or extension IDs

evals.prompt:
Our test team is triaging requirement snippets from different squads. For each snippet below, tell me which test design technique you would use and why. I only need the technique choice, not the test cases themselves. Save it as a markdown file.

1. Coupon code length must be 6 to 10 characters inclusive.
2. Applicant type can be employee, contractor, or guest. Guests are rejected. Employees and contractors may continue.
3. A transfer is allowed only when the source account is active, the destination account is active, and the amount is below the risk threshold.
4. Search results depend on browser, locale, sort order, and membership tier; exhaustive coverage is too large.
5. An order can move from Draft to Submitted to Paid to Shipped, and cancellation is legal only before shipment.
6. Given a registered shopper, when they apply a valid gift card during checkout, then the order total is reduced and the remaining balance is shown.
7. UC-12 Reset password: the user requests a link, opens it and sets a new password. Extensions: an unknown email shows a neutral message; a link older than 24 hours is refused.
8. Story PBI-2231. AC1: the voucher code is 8 to 12 alphanumeric characters. AC2: gold members get 10% off orders of EUR 50 or more, silver members 5%, others nothing. AC3: a voucher can be redeemed once and cannot be used after expiry.
9. AC-4: Given a shopper, when the basket total is EUR 50 or more, then shipping is free.
10. (The analyst explicitly asked for a decision table for this one.) Applicant type can be employee, contractor or guest; guests are rejected.
11. Defect BUG-5812: carts with exactly 10 items do not get the 5% bulk discount; REQ-DISC-3 says 10 or more items get 5% off.
